title: Heterogeneous treatment effects by firm size in DID

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
Difference-in-differences (DID) with heterogeneous treatment effects. The treatment is the larger tax cut received by large firms (treated=1) compared to small firms (treated=0) in the post-period (period 4+). The key assumption is parallel trends: absent the differential treatment, large and small firms would have followed parallel investment trends. We'll test this with pre-treatment trend analysis and estimate the average treatment effect on the treated (ATT).

## 2. R Code
```r
# Load required libraries
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(broom)
library(fixest)

# Read the data
data <- read.csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s09_data.csv")

# Add size_group variable for clarity
data$size_group <- ifelse(data$treated == 1, "Large", "Small")

# Basic DID regression
did_model <- lm(y ~ treated + post + treat_x_post, data = data)
summary(did_model)

# Extract and print the main coefficient
did_coeff <- coef(did_model)["treat_x_post"]
did_se <- summary(did_model)$coefficients["treat_x_post", "Std. Error"]
cat("Main DID Coefficient (ATT):", round(did_coeff, 4), 
    "(SE:", round(did_se, 4), ")\n")

# More flexible specification with period fixed effects
did_fe <- feols(y ~ treat_x_post | unit_id + period, data = data)
summary(did_fe)
cat("DID with Fixed Effects:", round(coef(did_fe)["treat_x_post"], 4), "\n")

# Pre-treatment trend test (parallel trends assumption)
pre_data <- data[data$period <= 3, ]
trend_test <- lm(y ~ treated * period, data = pre_data)
trend_coeff <- coef(trend_test)["treated:period"]
trend_pval <- summary(trend_test)$coefficients["treated:period", "Pr(>|t|)"]
cat("Pre-treatment trend coefficient:", round(trend_coeff, 4), 
    "p-value:", round(trend_pval, 4), "\n")

# Event study specification
data$rel_period <- data$period - 4
event_study <- feols(y ~ i(rel_period, treated, ref = -1) | unit_id + period, 
                     data = data)
summary(event_study)

# Calculate average treatment effects by period
post_periods <- 4:8
att_by_period <- sapply(post_periods, function(p) {
  period_data <- data[data$period == p, ]
  mean(period_data$y[period_data$treated == 1]) - 
  mean(period_data$y[period_data$treated == 0])
})
names(att_by_period) <- paste("Period", post_periods)
cat("ATT by period:\n")
print(round(att_by_period, 4))

# Robustness: Placebo test with fake treatment at period 2
data$fake_post <- ifelse(data$period >= 2, 1, 0)
data$fake_treat_x_post <- data$treated * data$fake_post
placebo_data <- data[data$period <= 3, ]
placebo_model <- lm(y ~ treated + fake_post + fake_treat_x_post, 
                    data = placebo_data)
placebo_coeff <- coef(placebo_model)["fake_treat_x_post"]
placebo_pval <- summary(placebo_model)$coefficients["fake_treat_x_post", "Pr(>|t|)"]
cat("Placebo test coefficient:", round(placebo_coeff, 4), 
    "p-value:", round(placebo_pval, 4), "\n")

# Summary of key results
cat("\n=== SUMMARY OF RESULTS ===\n")
cat("Main DID Estimate (ATT):", round(did_coeff, 4), "\n")
cat("Standard Error:", round(did_se, 4), "\n")
cat("95% CI: [", round(did_coeff - 1.96*did_se, 4), ",", 
    round(did_coeff + 1.96*did_se, 4), "]\n")
cat("Statistical Significance:", ifelse(abs(did_coeff/did_se) > 1.96, "Yes", "No"), "\n")
cat("Parallel Trends Test p-value:", round(trend_pval, 4), "\n")
cat("Placebo Test p-value:", round(placebo_pval, 4), "\n")
```

## 3. Expected Findings
I expect a positive coefficient of approximately 0.3-0.6 for the treatment effect. Large firms should increase investment more than small firms following the tax cut due to: (1) greater tax savings from the larger cut, (2) better access to capital markets to finance new investments, and (3) more sophisticated tax planning capabilities. The parallel trends test should show no significant pre-treatment differences (p > 0.05), and the placebo test should be insignificant, validating our identification strategy.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: DID with heterogeneous effects — triple-diff or interaction terms for size groups
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Large firms increase investment more than small firms post tax cut
_ground_truth.main_effect: 28% higher investment growth for large firms
